title: coap: Format text used in COL_INFO
description:
Use format_text_wsp() on strings from packet used in COL_INFO to
show non-printable characters as C-style escapes.

`format_text_wsp()` should allocate in `pinfo->pool`, so this string should never leak.
I will change to `format_text()` instead to explicit print newline as `\n`, maybe this will change the Coverity check.

`format_text()` and `format_text_wsp()` call the same internal function, so I wonder if that would change anything. It is supposed to be allocated in `pinfo->pool`, so it shouldn't leak.

Judging from the error message, I wonder if it's a false positive that would behave differently if the result were assigned to a `char*` before calling the column function, but that seems odd.
To be fair, it seems to be. But I have currently no idea how to tell coverity to stop looking for it. @geraldcombs or @crondaemon may have and idea about it though.

The causing issue is the following line of code:

![image](/uploads/ddb06b8e59241d44d563f126d62290de/image.png)

In my book, this is an issue as it is not covered by the pool? The question is, why does coverity think we are calling with a null-pointer?
It basically assumes, that pinfo->pool is NULL for whatever reason during the check.

I've read the modeling manual, but I didn't manage to use is. To read it, you have to log into coverity portal, then

https://scan.coverity.com/tune

and

https://scan.coverity.com/tune#writing-model

where you can find an explicit example to shut up a false positive for a leak.
